summary: NTILE divides ordered rows into a requested number of buckets.
documentation: NTILE divides ordered rows into a requested number of buckets. Bucket sizes differ by at most one, with larger buckets occurring first. Its output is a one-based bucket number, not a rank with tied scores grouped together.
inputs: A positive bucket count and window ordering.
returns: An integer bucket number for each row.
caution: A deterministic tie-breaker is needed for stable assignments. Equal scores may fall into different buckets.
scenarios: Divide an ordered review queue into balanced work batches.
Assign report rows to roughly equal score bands.
Split ordered customer accounts into fixed-number analysis groups.
title: Split a review queue into thirds
problem: From scores(id INTEGER, amount INTEGER), return id and NTILE(3) OVER (ORDER BY amount DESC, id) as bucket. Display by amount descending then id ascending. All fields are non-NULL, id is unique. Earlier buckets receive extra rows when needed.
goal: Use NTILE() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use a fixed bucket count of three and the same deterministic ordering for the window and final display.
